newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metway sees good year in prospect.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metway sees good year in prospect.

text.p: Metway Bank Ltd said business volumes in January and February were pleasing and that it was optimistic about a solid second-half result.
"Business volumes in January and February have been very pleasing. I am optimistic about the second half result," managing director Steve Jones told reporters.
"I think we are going to have a good year," Jones said.
Metway merged with the Queensland government owned Suncorp Finance and Insurance and the Queensland Industry Development Corp in November last year.

Earlier on Monday, Metway reported a 121 percent rise in operating profit for the half to A$73 million and a net profit of A$34 million. There was an pre-tax abnormal loss of A$23 million from write-off costs of a discontinued software project.

However, the company said the 162 percent rise in net profit for six months to December 31 was not indicative of the newly enlarged bank as the result included just one month from merger partners Suncorp and QIDC.
Jones said the combined Metway-Suncorp-QIDC group had identified about A$115 million annually to be gained from synergy initiatives and performance benefits in the next three years.
These savings would include rationalising "behind-the-branch" costs in retail banking and consolidating business banking activities, Jones said.
The combined group also intended to pool resources and reduce costs in corporate and support services while improving the profitability of the general insurance business, he said.
Metway shares closed 11 cents higher at A$5.77 on Monday.
